input.quote: Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale: Section 12.3 expressly preserves our freedom to develop, acquire, license, sell or use any product or service and to engage any supplier, and Vendor affirmatively acknowledges that we have made no exclusivity commitment. A full-document search for "exclusive", "sole", requirements-purchase and third-party-procurement language turned up no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation binding us: the remaining "exclusive" references are a non-exclusive licence to us (13.1), Vendor's Deliverable ownership (14.2), exclusive-remedy and exclusive-forum provisions (19.4, 21.4, 28.1-28.2) — none of which restrict our sourcing. Section 7.2's obligation to disclose and match a more favourable offer before engaging another provider is a right-to-match/MFN mechanic; it does not prohibit engaging an alternative provider once honoured, and belongs under MFN rather than being double-flagged here. The take-or-pay commitment in 2.1 is a volume commitment for MINCOMMIT, not exclusive dealing. The clause therefore meets the preferred position, so no redline is proposed.
